expectedText:
CALIFORNIA LLC ANNUAL FEE — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Acme, LLC

PURPOSE AND SCOPE OF THIS INFORMATION SHEET
This information sheet, prepared by Jordan Lee, states what California's Revenue and Taxation Code provides about the separate LLC fee imposed by Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 17942 — a state fee, based on a limited liability company's total income, that is distinct from the flat $800 annual minimum franchise tax imposed by Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 17941. Where a specific business name is named below, that is Acme, LLC; this sheet can also be read on its own, without it filled in, as a general reference to what the statute says. This sheet states the law; it does not calculate, estimate, or evaluate what any particular limited liability company owes, and it is not a substitute for individualized legal or tax advice.

WHO THE LLC FEE APPLIES TO
The § 17942 fee is imposed on "every limited liability company subject to tax under Section 17941" — and § 17941 itself defines "limited liability company," for its own purposes, to exclude an organization "that is not taxable as a corporation for California tax purposes." An organization formed as an LLC under state law but that has elected, or is otherwise taxable, as a corporation for California tax purposes falls outside that definition, and so outside the tax and fee imposed by this chapter.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "In addition to the tax imposed under Section 17941, every limited liability company subject to tax under Section 17941 shall pay annually to this state a fee equal to:"
  — Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 17942(a), Tax and Fees on Limited Liability Companies, imposition of the LLC fee (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=RTC&sectionNum=17942.)
  "For purposes of this section, “limited liability company” means an organization, other than a limited liability company that is exempt from the tax and fees imposed under this chapter pursuant to Section 23701h or Section 23701x, that is formed by one or more persons under the law of this state, any other country, or any other state, as a “limited liability company” and that is not taxable as a corporation for California tax purposes."
  — Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 17941(d), Tax and Fees on Limited Liability Companies, definition of "limited liability company" for purposes of the chapter (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=RTC&sectionNum=17941.)
  Known gap: This is the statute's own definitional language, not a restatement of federal "check-the-box" terminology; the statute does not use the words "partnership" or "disregarded entity" in this definition. This document does not independently verify how the Franchise Tax Board applies this exclusion to every possible LLC tax election scenario, and it does not address any particular company's own tax classification, which is addressed by this project's separate Operating Agreement documents. Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code §§ 17941 and 17942 are two separate, independently numbered sections; the two citations below are independent of one another.

THE LLC FEE IS OWED IN ADDITION TO THE $800 MINIMUM TAX
The § 17942 LLC fee does not replace or offset the flat annual tax imposed by § 17941 (currently $800, per the amount set by Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 23153(d)(1) and cross-referenced by § 17941(a)) — the statute's own text imposes the fee "[i]n addition to" that tax. A limited liability company within the fee's income brackets owes both amounts: the flat annual tax under § 17941, and the separate, income-tiered fee under § 17942.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "In addition to the tax imposed under Section 17941, every limited liability company subject to tax under Section 17941 shall pay annually to this state a fee equal to:"
  — Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 17942(a), Tax and Fees on Limited Liability Companies, the LLC fee is imposed in addition to the § 17941 tax (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=RTC&sectionNum=17942.)
  "for each taxable year beginning on or after January 1, 1997, a limited liability company doing business in this state (as defined in Section 23101) shall pay annually to this state a tax for the privilege of doing business in this state in an amount equal to the applicable amount specified in subdivision (d) of Section 23153 for the taxable year."
  — Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 17941(a), Tax and Fees on Limited Liability Companies, the annual tax for doing business in the state (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=RTC&sectionNum=17941.)
  Known gap: This document does not restate every detail of the § 17941 annual tax itself, including its due date, its continuing obligation until dissolution, or recent statutory amendments to it — those are addressed by this project's LLC Articles of Organization document. Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code §§ 17941 and 17942 are two separate, independently numbered sections; the two citations below are independent of one another.

THE FEE SCHEDULE
The LLC fee is set on a tiered schedule keyed to total income: $900 at total income of $250,000 or more (but less than $500,000); $2,500 at $500,000 or more (but less than $1,000,000); $6,000 at $1,000,000 or more (but less than $5,000,000); and $11,790 at $5,000,000 or more. An LLC with total income below $250,000 owes no fee under this section (though it may still owe the separate $800 minimum tax addressed elsewhere in this project).

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "(1) Nine hundred dollars ($900), if the total income from all sources derived from or attributable to this state for the taxable year is two hundred fifty thousand dollars ($250,000) or more, but less than five hundred thousand dollars ($500,000). (2) Two thousand five hundred dollars ($2,500), if the total income from all sources derived from or attributable to this state for the taxable year is five hundred thousand dollars ($500,000) or more, but less than one million dollars ($1,000,000). (3) Six thousand dollars ($6,000), if the total income from all sources derived from or attributable to this state for the taxable year is one million dollars ($1,000,000) or more, but less than five million dollars ($5,000,000). (4) Eleven thousand seven hundred ninety dollars ($11,790), if the total income from all sources derived from or attributable to this state for the taxable year is five million dollars ($5,000,000) or more."
  — Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 17942(a)(1)–(4), Tax and Fees on Limited Liability Companies, the tiered LLC fee schedule (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=RTC&sectionNum=17942.)
  Known gap: This is the fee schedule as codified in Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 17942(a)(1)–(4) as of this verification date; it does not reflect any inflation adjustment or amendment enacted after that date. This document does not calculate any particular company's total income or which bracket it falls into.

"TOTAL INCOME" MEANS GROSS INCOME, NOT NET PROFIT
"Total income from all sources" is not net profit. The statute defines it as gross income — as gross income is defined for California corporation tax purposes, which itself adopts the federal Internal Revenue Code's definition of gross income — plus the cost of goods sold paid or incurred in the taxpayer's trade or business. Business expenses, deductions, and losses that would reduce net profit generally do not reduce this figure; a company can owe a substantial LLC fee for a year in which it had little or no net profit, if its gross income was high enough.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "“total income from all sources derived from or attributable to this state” means gross income, as defined in Section 24271, plus the cost of goods sold that are paid or incurred in connection with the trade or business of the taxpayer."
  — Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 17942(b)(1)(A), Tax and Fees on Limited Liability Companies, definition of "total income from all sources" (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=RTC&sectionNum=17942.)
  "Section 61 of the Internal Revenue Code, relating to gross income defined, shall apply, except as otherwise provided."
  — Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 24271(a), Gross Income, adoption of the federal Internal Revenue Code definition (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=RTC&sectionNum=24271.)
  Known gap: This document quotes the statute's cross-reference to "gross income, as defined in Section 24271" and Section 24271's own text, which in turn adopts Internal Revenue Code § 61's definition of gross income; this document does not independently trace or quote 26 U.S.C. § 61 itself. Section 17942(b)(1)(A) also excludes certain LLC-to-LLC allocations from this figure and, in 17942(b)(1)(B), ties the sourcing rules to Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code §§ 25135–25137 — provisions on assigning sales to California that this document does not independently restate. Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code §§ 17942 and 24271 are two separate, independently numbered sections; the two citations below are independent of one another.

THE FEE IS PAID BY ESTIMATE, MID-YEAR
The LLC fee is not paid after the year closes, the way the underlying return is filed — the statute requires it to be estimated and paid on or before the 15th day of the sixth month of the current taxable year (for a calendar-year LLC, June 15), based on the LLC's estimate of its own total income for that year. A 10% penalty applies to any underpayment of that estimate, unless the amount paid by that date is at least equal to the LLC's total fee for the preceding taxable year.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "The fee assessed under this section shall be due and payable on the date the return of the limited liability company is required to be filed under Section 18633.5, shall be collected and refunded in the same manner as the taxes imposed by this part, and shall be subject to interest and applicable penalties."
  — Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 17942(c), Tax and Fees on Limited Liability Companies, when the fee is due (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=RTC&sectionNum=17942.)
  "The fee imposed by this section shall be estimated and paid on or before the 15th day of the sixth month of the current taxable year."
  — Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 17942(d)(1), Tax and Fees on Limited Liability Companies, the mid-year estimate requirement (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=RTC&sectionNum=17942.)
  Known gap: This document does not independently trace Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 18633.5 (the return-filing provision cross-referenced for the fee's ultimate due date and for identifying which LLCs must file that return) or the FTB's own form instructions for the estimate payment (commonly made using FTB Form 3536); it states only what §§ 17942(c) and (d) themselves say about timing. Subdivisions (c) and (d) quoted below are both part of the same section, Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 17942, and are not independent of one another.

SIGNATURE AND CERTIFICATION
I, Jordan Lee, certify that I prepared this information sheet as a summary of Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 17942 and the statutes it cross-references, for informational reference only. This information sheet does not calculate any amount owed, does not evaluate Acme, LLC's total income or fee bracket, and is not a substitute for consulting a person licensed to practice law or provide tax advice in the relevant jurisdiction.

Business name under consideration, if applicable: Acme, LLC

Executed on September 4, 2026 at San Jose, California.

Signature of Jordan Lee: ☐ _________________________
